verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's own AI Object Storage documents S3-compatible access for training data and model weights. It adds an acceleration layer (LOTA, usable from GPU and CPU Nodes, with cache warming) and Cloud Console upload/download, so the core of efficient data movement is covered. However, the evidence shows no cloud-storage sync or cross-cloud migration tooling, and efficiency claims are vendor-only. Missing for 10: documented sync/migration tooling from other clouds (e.g., bulk transfer or rclone/s5cmd guides), detailed S3 endpoint/API compatibility documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration of transfer performance.

support.subject: As a developer, I can move data in and out efficiently — S3-compatible endpoints, cloud-storage sync, or documented transfer tooling

citations.quote: Store training data, checkpoints, and model weights with efficient S3-compatible access directly to your GPU compute resources.
CPU-only clusters can now use the LOTA endpoint for accelerated object storage access.
Training jobs that start with a warm cache can see a 30-50% faster first epoch compared to cold reads.
You can now browse, upload, download, and manage objects in CoreWeave AI Object Storage buckets directly from the CoreWeave Cloud Console
you can now exchange that token directly for temporary AI Object Storage credentials through the container credentials endpoint.
